beats: Hook: end of 2023, the manager wants a 405-billion-parameter model trained in four months; on one GPU it would take 584 years (slide 10) (line_train_giant_order, MANAGER as in line_manager_2; chefs = GPUs as in line_d_chefs).

First step, before any GPU: a back-of-the-envelope total; Chinchilla says ~20 tokens per parameter and Llama 3 went past it (15T / 405B ~ 37) to make serving cheaper (her words, slide 11) (line_train_envelope_sums).
Why the pressure only grows: scaling laws, bigger models and more data give lower loss (slide 9) (line_grow).
The bill in FLOPs: 6 x 405B x 15T = 3.645 x 10^25 (slide 11) (line_train_chef_mountain, line_heap).
Why 6: forward 2, backward 4 (gradients for the input and for the weights) (L05 3) (line_train_two_pots).
One H100 at 1,979 TFLOPS (FP8 peak): 1.84 x 10^10 s = 584 years (slide 12) (line_train_long_beard, line_train_calendar_flurry, line_gpu).
Reality, ~54 days: ~40% utilisation from waiting and failures (line_train_waiting_chefs, line_train_blown_fuse) and 16-bit instead of FP8 (line_train_scoop_spoon) (slide 13).
Takeaway + next: training has to be distributed; first the hardware ladder (L04-02), then four ways to cut the job (L04-03).

The chef holds the top end with both hands, eyes wide, mouth open. Landscape image 1536x1024; the two characters and the ticket fill about 90% of the width and about 85% of the height. The ticket is blank paper. No text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logos anywhere.
